items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a locally finite $k$-linear abelian rigid monoidal category whose tensor product is $k$-bilinear and whose tensor unit $\mathbf1$ satisfies $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)\cong k$. Here rigid means every object has left and right duals with evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying the two snake identities. Equip $\mathcal C$ with a braiding $c_{Y,Z}:Y\otimes Z\to Z\otimes Y$, natural in $Y,Z$, satisfying the two hexagon identities with the associator $\alpha$. Fix $X\in\mathcal C$, put $P_0(X)=\mathbf1$, $P_1(X)=X$, and recursively put $P_{m+1}(X)=P_m(X)\otimes X$.

For each $n\ge2$ and $1\le i<n$, let $Q_{n,i}(X)$ be the parenthesized product $\bigl(P_{i-1}(X)\otimes(X\otimes X)\bigr)\otimes P_{n-i-1}(X)$, with the unit factors at either end removed by the fixed unitors when an exponent is zero. Choose a canonical rebracketing isomorphism $\rho_{n,i}:P_n(X)\to Q_{n,i}(X)$ made from associators, unitors, and their inverses, without permuting the ordered tensor factors. Define

$$B_i^X:=\rho_{n,i}^{-1}\circ\bigl(\operatorname{id}_{P_{i-1}(X)}\otimes c_{X,X}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{P_{n-i-1}(X)}\bigr)\circ\rho_{n,i}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(P_n(X)).$$

The family $B_i^X$ is independent of the chosen canonical rebracketing path and determines a homomorphism $\varrho_n:B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(P_n(X))$, where $B_n$ is the braid group with positive generator $\sigma_i$ sent to $B_i^X$. These are exact algebraic morphisms.

**Physical interpretation boundary.** A physical adiabatic-exchange interpretation needs additional data: a specified Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a path $K(s)$, $s\in[0,1]$, of self-adjoint operators on a stated common domain; a Borel set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R$ for which the spectral projection $P(s)=\mathbf1_\Omega(K(s))$ has finite rank and $\operatorname{dist}(\Omega,\sigma(K(s))\setminus\Omega)\ge\gamma>0$ uniformly in $s$; a connection $\nabla$ on the vector bundle with fibers $\operatorname{ran}P(s)$, which specifies parallel transport; and an explicit operator-norm error bound comparing that transport with the exact evolution in a stated slow-evolution regime. In a physical realization, $K(s)$ and $\gamma$ have the model's energy units; no value is fixed here. The categorical data supply none of this and do not assert an experimental realization.

items.title: Vacuum projectors obey the reverse adjacent Temperley–Lieb relation

references.title: Joshua Chen, The Temperley–Lieb Categories and Skein Modules, ANU Honours Thesis (2014)
references.locator: §2.2, Remark 2.2.3: both adjacent Temperley–Lieb projector relations; the local reverse relation is derived from the supplied normalized anyonic F-coefficient.

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects, with $a$ self-dual, $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$, and supply the normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum with sign $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and positive spherical dimension $d_a$. For $n\ge3$, take the fixed-boundary repeated-$a$ path space $H_{a,n;b,c}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n)$ with $T_0=b$ and $T_{j+1}=T_j\otimes a$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Let $P_i=P_{i,\mathbf1}$ be the orthogonal local vacuum-channel projectors and put $U_i=\delta_aP_i$, where $\delta_a=\kappa_ad_a$. Then, for every $1\le i\le n-2$,

$$U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}.$$

This supplies the reverse adjacent relation for the repeated-charge Temperley–Lieb family.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $V$ be a complex vector space, and let $U_1,\ldots,U_{n-1}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$. Suppose $\delta\in\mathbb C$, $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, and assume

$$U_i^2=\delta U_i,\qquad U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i,\qquad U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad U_iU_j=U_jU_i\quad(|i-j|>1).$$

Define $B_i:=qI_V-U_i$. Then each $B_i$ is invertible with $B_i^{-1}=q^{-1}I_V-U_i$; the $B_i$ satisfy the Artin braid and far-commutation relations; and

$$(B_i-qI_V)(B_i+q^{-1}I_V)=0.$$

Thus $\sigma_i\mapsto B_i$ defines a group homomorphism $B_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. If $H_v(n)$ is the generic type-A Hecke algebra with $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, its scalar specialization $H_{q^2}(n)$ has a unital algebra representation $T_i\mapsto qB_i$. This is the standard Hecke normalization because $(qB_i-q^2I_V)(qB_i+I_V)=0$. If $V$ is a complex Hilbert space and each $U_i$ is bounded self-adjoint, then $\delta\in\mathbb R$ and $|q|=1$ imply that each $B_i$ is unitary. No faithfulness, diagonalizability, or physical realization is asserted.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, $V$ be a complex vector space, $U_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $\delta\in\mathbb C$, and $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ satisfy $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and

$$U_i^2=\delta U_i,\qquad U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i,\qquad U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1},\qquad U_iU_j=U_jU_i\quad(|i-j|>1).$$

Put $B_i=qI_V-U_i$, and let $\rho_n:B_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ be the homomorphism $\rho_n(\sigma_i)=B_i$ from the preceding Temperley–Lieb–Hecke construction. At $q=1$ one has $\delta=2$ and $B_i=I_V-U_i$. These operators satisfy $B_i^2=I_V$, so $\rho_n$ factors through the canonical quotient $\pi_n:B_n\to S_n$ as a representation $S_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. The $q=1$ Hecke generator relations are then the type-A Coxeter relations. For general $q$, the roots of the quadratic relation are $q$ and $-q^{-1}$; they coincide when $q^2=-1$, and no diagonalizability is asserted. Involutivity is not imposed by the Hecke relation and need not hold.

items.title: Vacuum-channel exchange operator on its invariant subspaces

references.title: Joshua Chen, The Temperley-Lieb categories and skein modules, ANU Honours Thesis, 2014
references.locator: §§2.1–2.3: the cup/cap convention, loop parameter, and Temperley-Lieb projectors.

items.statement: Let $a$ be a self-dual simple site charge in a unitary spherical fusion category, with one-dimensional vacuum fusion $a\otimes a\to\mathbf1$, and take a repeated-$a$ fusion-path space $V$ and an applicable interior index $i$. Let $P_i=P_{i,\mathbf1}$ be the orthogonal vacuum-channel projector, with the supplied normalized Frobenius–Schur sign $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$, positive dimension $d_a$, and signed loop parameter $\delta_a=\kappa_ad_a$. Suppose $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ satisfies $q+q^{-1}=\delta_a$. For $U_i=\delta_aP_i$ and $B_i=qI_V-U_i$, $B_i$ acts as $-q^{-1}I_V$ on $\operatorname{ran}P_i$ and as $qI_V$ on $\ker P_i$. If either subspace is zero, its listed scalar is not an eigenvalue contributed by that subspace. The equation gives an algebraic channel action only; it does not identify $B_i$ with an experimentally realized adiabatic exchange.
